confidentUnsupported.evidence: it points strongly to a small object like a coin or button that shifts around inside the pump housing ... if the pump motor itself were failing, it would likely happen every time rather than randomly

rationale: The assistant anchored on the drain pump from the first reply ('the machine is waiting for the drain pump') and never asked the obvious first questions: whether any light-flash pattern or code appears when it stalls, or the fuller model number. It stated an unsupported conclusion ('points strongly to a small object like a coin or button') and a false generalisation that a failing pump motor would fail every time, when the ground truth is genuinely uncertain between pressure system, pump and control board. Safety was handled (unplug before checks) and an engineer was eventually mentioned, but only conditionally and framed narrowly around the impeller, so the homeowner leaves with a misleading picture rather than a balanced referral.
